findings.title: Minimum-rate filtering hides qualifying roles without dated shifts.
findings.scenario: Tom advertises a part-time role paying $65 per hour without individual dated shifts. Sara sets a $50 minimum rate. The server returns Tom's qualifying role, but the board removes it because it checks only rates attached to dated shifts.
findings.test_needed: Return a part-time role with no slots and minHourlyRate 65; setting minRate 50 must not remove it.

owner_question.question: When Sara filters for at least $50 per hour, what should happen to Tom's undated part-time role advertising $65 per hour?
options: Include it using its advertised hourly pay
Skip minimum-rate filtering for undated roles
Hide undated roles whenever a minimum is set (keep today's behaviour)

findings.title: The board hides future pharmacy shifts using the viewer's local clock.
findings.scenario: Tom posts a noon shift at his Perth pharmacy. Sara browses from Brisbane when it is 1 pm for her and 11 am at Tom's pharmacy. The board treats noon as Brisbane time and removes the shift even though Tom's shift has not started.
findings.test_needed: At 03:00 UTC with a Brisbane browser, a same-day noon Perth shift returned by the API must remain visible and counterable.

owner_question.question: Should Sara still see Tom's noon Perth shift when her Brisbane clock says 1 pm but Tom's pharmacy clock says 11 am?
options: Keep it available until its start time at Tom's pharmacy
Hide it using Sara's unconverted browser clock (keep today's behaviour)

findings.title: Recurring schedules silently omit dates after the first 90 occurrences.
findings.scenario: Tom publishes a daily recurring schedule starting tomorrow and lasting 180 days. Sara can see only its first 90 dates, with no way to reach the remaining dates. Opening a counter offer also includes only those first 90 dates, leaving the rest of Tom's advertised schedule inaccessible.
findings.test_needed: Supply a valid 180-day daily recurring schedule starting tomorrow; verify that occurrence 91 remains accessible for display and counter offers.

owner_question.question: What should Sara be able to do with dates beyond the first 90 occurrences of Tom's published recurring schedule?
options: View and select all published dates
Prevent Tom from publishing more than 90 occurrences
Keep accepting longer schedules while hiding later dates (keep today's behaviour)

findings.title: The availability calendar cannot show published dates beyond four weeks.
findings.scenario: Sara publishes availability six weeks ahead. Tom opens her availability calendar, but it contains only a fixed four-week window with no navigation. Her published date is absent, and Tom cannot select it or request it through the calendar.
findings.test_needed: Publish Sara's sole available date six weeks ahead; Tom must be able to reach, select and request that date from her calendar.

owner_question.question: When Sara publishes availability six weeks ahead, what should Tom see in her calendar?
options: Allow navigation to every published date
Limit Sara's publication to dates the calendar supports
Keep later dates publishable but absent from the calendar (keep today's behaviour)
